evidence.quote: {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:-<ety:bor<fro:putride<ety:der<la:putridus>>><la:putridus>>|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*puH-}} From {{inh|en|enm|-}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|putride}} or directly from {{der|en|la|putridus||rotten, decayed}}, from {{m|la|putreō||to be rotten or putrid}}, from {{m|la|puter||rotten, decaying, putrid}}.

"festering gangrenous, in a state of decay," from Old French putride and directly from… See origin and meaning of putrid. from Old French putride and directly from Latin putridus , from putrere "to rot," from putris "rotten, crumbling," related to putere "to stink," from PIE root *pu- (2) "to rot, stink" (see pus ).
